did_you_know.text: Did you know? Moab rebelled against Israel after Ahab’s death, as stated at the beginning of the chapter.

Did you know? Ahaziah was injured after falling through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria. Instead of turning to the Lord, he sent messengers to inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron, asking whether he would recover.
Did you know? The angel of the Lord sent Elijah to meet the king’s messengers and rebuke them for turning to the god of Ekron instead of seeking the God of Israel.
Did you know? The message delivered to Ahaziah was unequivocal: he would not get off the bed onto which he had climbed; he would die because he had sent to inquire of Baal-Zebub.
Did you know? The messengers described the man they had met as “a hairy man” wearing a leather belt; from this description, the king recognized that he was Elijah the Tishbite.
Did you know? Ahaziah sent a captain with fifty soldiers to Elijah, and the captain ordered him in the king’s name to come down from the mountaintop.
Did you know? Elijah declared that if he was a man of God, fire would come down from heaven—and indeed, the fire consumed the first captain and his fifty men.
Did you know? The second delegation, consisting of a captain and fifty men, was also punished with fire from heaven after the captain ordered Elijah to come down.
Did you know? The third captain did not order Elijah to do anything; instead, he knelt before him and pleaded for his own life and the lives of his men, showing humility and reverence.

Did you know? Ahaziah died according to the word of the Lord, and since he had no son, his brother Jehoram succeeded him as king. The rest of Ahaziah’s deeds are recorded in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.
